A letter for you

Happy Birthday, Renuka

My dearest Renuka,

Happy birthday. Today the whole world should slow down and smile a little, because the day you were born was a quiet gift to everyone lucky enough to know you.

I don’t know whether you ever noticed me in college — I was just one more face in the crowd. But to me, you were never one of the many. Every single day you would walk in with that same bright, laughing smile — never a harsh word, never an angry face. You will never know how much that one smile quietly did for my day.

In college life we pass by so many people — girls, boys, classmates, seniors — and most of them blur into one. But a person whose heart is truly pure, whose kindness carries no price, comes along only once. You are that one. Anyone can be beautiful on the outside; you are beautiful where it truly counts, and that is a thousand times rarer.

And here is the strangest, truest thing of all. In that whole crowd, we are lucky if we ever meet even one person who feels like a reflection of our own soul — someone who seems like a copy of who we are inside. In my college life, I found that person. It was you. That is why your birthday is not only your day; a small piece of it belongs to me too.

So today I only want to say this: stay exactly as you are — that laugh, that heart, that light you carry without even knowing it. You are the best friend my own heart chose for itself. May this year give back to you, a hundred times over, everything you quietly give to others. Happy birthday once again, with all of my heart. 🎂 🎈

— With all my heart, your friend.
— G.Shanak

Designer / Creator / AI Educator / Founder @ Singapore

About

Meng To is a designer, creator, and AI educator based in Singapore. He is the founder of Design+Code, where for over a decade he has taught designers and developers to build real apps — from Sketch and Xcode through SwiftUI, and now the AI tools that let one person ship what used to take a team. His work lives on the seam between craft and code: teaching designers to build, and builders to see. This sketchbook is the other half of that — the city looked at slowly, in ink and a little colour: shophouse shutters, hawker tents, the bay at dusk.
